about.title: Calexico Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product can cause serious harm in an instant, whether it's a malfunctioning tool at a warehouse near Rt 98, a faulty vehicle part on Cesar Chavez, or an appliance that fails at home. Calexico sits at a border crossing point with steady commercial and consumer traffic, meaning products move through the area constantly from many different manufacturers, distributors, and retailers. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a strict liability claim, which means the focus is on whether the product itself was defective rather than whether a company was negligent. That said, these cases often involve multiple parties and require preserving the product as evidence early on. If a defective product has hurt you or someone you love in Calexico, LawProactive can connect you at no cost with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options going forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Product Liability Cases Work Differently

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Proof
items.desc: Under California law, you generally don't have to prove a manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may open more than one path toward accountability.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters Early
items.desc: Keeping the defective item intact and unaltered is often critical to building a strong claim, so acting quickly can make a real difference.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California generally allows strict liability claims for defective products, which focus on whether the product itself was unreasonably dangerous rather than on the manufacturer's conduct. An independent attorney can explain how this standard applies to your specific situation.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including any packaging, parts, or instructions. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away, since the product itself is often key evidence in these claims.

items.question: Is a product liability claim different if I live near the Calexico border area?
items.answer: The underlying California law is the same, but products sold or distributed through border-adjacent commerce in Imperial County can sometimes involve additional manufacturers or importers. An independent attorney can help sort out which parties may be responsible in your case.
